mappings.note: Which cities National Highway No. 1 links: a road mode and the route by which it knits regions together, LO-6. Not LO-7, since no trade or tourism value is weighed.
The navigable stretch of National Waterway No. 1: an inland water mode and its route, LO-6.
The biggest port with a natural, well-sheltered harbour: a sea-transport node, LO-6. C-2.3-LO-19 would need the trade carried through it to be analysed.
The subsidiary port built to relieve Kolkata (Haldia): port infrastructure within the transport network, LO-6.
What counts as first-class mail: the communication half of LO-6, which the chapter treats alongside transport.
India's southernmost international airport: an air-transport node, LO-6.
The oldest port on the eastern coast: port infrastructure, LO-6, not the trade it handles.
Where narrow gauge lines survive: rail as a mode of transport, LO-6.
Which claim is not an advantage of pipelines: still a description of the pipeline mode and what it does for the economy, LO-6. Not C-2.3, since no data are interpreted.
The Border Roads Organisation as builder of border roads: the institutional side of the road network, LO-6.
Which port is tidal (Kandla): port type within the transport network, LO-6.
Duplicate stem of qid:106075; the port developed to relieve Kolkata, LO-6.
The two extremes of the North-South Corridor: a highway route knitting the country end to end, LO-6.
The oldest artificial port: port infrastructure recall, LO-6.
Who builds and maintains National Highways: the institutional side of the road mode, as with qid:106081.
Pipelines as the mode that cuts trans-shipment loss and delay for petroleum and gas: a mode and its function, LO-6.
Pawan Hans as ONGC's offshore helicopter operator: a specialised air-transport service, LO-6.
The language with the most newspaper titles: the mass-communication half of LO-6.
Which claim about India's sea ports is untrue: port infrastructure, LO-6, not the trade passing through them.

What India now earns large foreign exchange by exporting: the role of international trade in India's economy, LO-19. Not LO-20, which requires a balance of trade to be interpreted, and not LO-6, since no transport mode is at issue.
India's nationalised airline: an air-transport operator, LO-6.
The oldest artificial and second most important port: duplicate target of qid:106085 with the ranking added, LO-6.
